issues.legal_issue: A complaint cannot be quashed at the prima facie stage merely because a related civil dispute is pending, without examining whether the complaint’s allegations make out the alleged offences.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that the accused committed offences involving voluntarily causing hurt and theft with common intention.
The Magistrate found a prima facie case and took cognizance.
The High Court quashed the complaint after emphasizing the pending landlord-tenant and property disputes, without determining whether the complaint’s allegations made out the alleged offences.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order was legally unsustainable because it did not assess the complaint’s allegations; the Magistrate’s order taking cognizance was restored.
issues.legal_principle: At the stage of deciding whether a prima facie case is made out, the court must examine the allegations in the complaint. Mere pendency of a civil suit does not answer whether the alleged criminal offences are made out. The Court referred to State of Haryana v. Ch. Bhajan Lal (AIR 1992 SC 604), which the High Court had cited but failed to apply. The alleged offences were under Sections 323 and 379 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

rule.if: complaint_quashing_proceeding and complaint_alleges_criminal_offences and quashing_court_relies_on_civil_dispute and not quashing_court_assesses_complaint_allegations

predicates.complaint_quashing_proceeding: A complaint alleging criminal offences is challenged for quashing before trial.
predicates.complaint_alleges_criminal_offences: The complainant sets out allegations that the accused committed criminal offences.
predicates.quashing_court_relies_on_civil_dispute: The court quashing the complaint relies on a related civil dispute as a basis for its decision.
predicates.quashing_court_assesses_complaint_allega: The court quashing the complaint examines whether the allegations make out a prima facie case for the alleged offences.

issues.definition: When a court is asked to quash a complaint alleging criminal offences, reliance on a related civil dispute without assessing the complaint’s allegations makes the quashing order legally unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A court considering quashing before trial cannot assess contradictions or inconsistencies in witness statements, because those matters are for evaluation at trial.
material_facts: The High Court quashed the complaint before trial.
In doing so, the High Court relied on alleged contradictions in witnesses’ statements about the occurrence.
The evidence had not yet been fully adduced at trial.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had no jurisdiction in the quashing proceeding to appreciate the evidence by assessing contradictions in witness statements; those matters were for the Magistrate at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, a court considering whether to quash proceedings before trial cannot undertake appreciation of evidence, including deciding whether witness statements contain contradictions or inconsistencies. Such matters are to be considered by the trial court after the parties adduce evidence.

predicates.pretrial_quashing_proceeding: A court is considering whether to quash a criminal proceeding before the evidence is adduced at trial.
predicates.quashing_court_assesses_witness_contradi: The court considering quashing evaluates contradictions or inconsistencies in witness statements.

issues.definition: When a court considers quashing before trial and evaluates contradictions in witness statements, those contradictions must instead be assessed at trial.
